title: The Unforgiving Servant
text:
Peter asked Jesus how often he should forgive someone who wronged him. As many as seven times? Not seven times, Jesus said, but seventy-seven times, and he told a story.

A king decided to settle accounts with his servants. One of them owed him ten thousand talents, a sum so vast he could never repay it. The king ordered that the man, his wife, his children and everything he owned be sold. The servant fell on his knees and begged, "Be patient with me, and I will pay you everything." The king took pity on him, released him and cancelled the entire debt.

That same servant went out and met a fellow servant who owed him a hundred denarii, a small amount. He seized him by the throat and demanded, "Pay what you owe!" The fellow servant fell down and begged in the very same words, "Be patient with me, and I will pay you." But he refused and had the man thrown into prison until he could pay.

The other servants were deeply troubled and told the king. The king summoned the man. "You wicked servant," he said. "I forgave you all that debt because you begged me. Should you not have had mercy on your fellow servant, as I had mercy on you?" In anger he handed him over to the jailers until he should pay back all he owed.
lesson: Remember how often you have been forgiven and given second chances. Let that memory shape how you treat people who owe or have wronged you.
people: A king, a servant, a fellow servant
